initial_failures.finding: Deep callbacks neither retained their owner context across threads nor denied dispatch after durable Stop.
Same-request approval retry could miss a newly committed admission before refusing a changed cache entry.
Registry drain ignored persistence spawned by finishing workers.

fixes: Capture the trusted deep-run identity and context in each of six built-in callbacks, copy that context for each invocation, and consult durable control before dispatch. Restore binding after worker exit; control-store errors deny dispatch.
Recheck original admission before returning a cached-plan refusal.
Drain newly spawned background work within the original total drain deadline; cancel unfinished children at that deadline.
native_coverage: Private canonical DB worker starts before Stop, then attempts an exec_shell callback after Stop. Underlying synthetic effect is denied; cancelled audit retains the late result and cost. Real-control browser approval/recovery cases also pass.
limits: Only runner-owned deep custom callbacks are bound here. Standalone/unbound deep-tool entry paths, arbitrary REPL code and framework-owned provider requests are not claimed gated. This does not establish general deep-framework authorization parity, process-death recovery or full acceptance. No production deployment.

broad_engine.selection: not slow and not integration and not llm and not e2e and not smoke
broad_engine.note: Single clean broad invocation after deep callback controls, approval cache-race fix and dynamic registry drain. Source code/tests unchanged during run; committed while it ran. Existing connect_tcp unawaited-coroutine warning remains; its collection location is not evidence of the initiating path.

checks: Ruff lint/format, Node syntax and diff checks pass; no size cap increased.
